Subject: Quick clarifications: retention windows and deletion semantics for Hosted API

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Ideally we'd get a table we can drop into our security questionnaire; we have an internal deadline of next Friday.

Topline questions:
- Are hosted customer request payloads stored outside the US for any purpose?
- Is there a configurable TTL per-tenant for retained request logs or user-provided data?
- If Lucent requests a full account erasure, what systems are touched and what is the expected completion time? (Please call out backups/snapshots.)

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary below; attaching a retention matrix and our SOC2 summary for context. If you want, Kimberly can add the low-level operational notes about backups and snapshot expiry.

1) Residency (hosted API)
- Primary: Customer requests processed in the region selected at account provisioning (for Lucent this is us-west-2).
- Secondary: For transient routing or model-variant fallback we do not persist customer request payloads outside the primary region. All persisted telemetry/usage logs tied to your tenant remain in the provisioned region unless otherwise requested under an enterprise contract.

2) Retention / TTL
- Default: 30 days for request/response payloads and API logs (applies to hosted self-serve tier).
- Enterprise: TTL is configurable for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted we support an exceptions process tied to an enterprise agreement where TTL can be shortened to 0-7 days depending on contract terms.
- Separate telemetry: aggregated telemetry for service metrics is retained 13 months; telemetry is pseudonymized and not linkable to raw request payloads.

3) Deletion / Erasure process
- Immediate steps on a customer erasure request: (a) mark tenant data for deletion in our control plane; (b) schedule in-region purge job which deletes primary KV-store entries and object store blobs associated with customer request/response data; (c) invalidate caches and remove cached prefix/KV entries.
- Backups/snapshots: Automated snapshots stored for disaster recovery are retained per retention schedule; we offer an expedited snapshot purge request for enterprise contracts. Standard snapshot retention is 30 days; snapshot deletion requests are processed within 5-7 business days under expedited workflows.
- Completion window: For hosted accounts with no special addendum, full erasure of accessible stores typically completes within 7 business days; backup purge (where applicable) can take up to 30 days unless an expedited process is agreed.

I've attached the retention matrix (lucent-retention-matrix.xlsx) showing the mapping of data types -> TTL -> retention location.

If that looks good, Kimberly will follow up with exact operational playbook language for the questionnaire items about backups and proof artifacts.

Best,
Jordan

Adding operational detail for Lucent's security questionnaire — feel free to paste the bullet answers into their doc.

Backups and snapshots (operational playbook)
- Snapshot cadence: daily incremental snapshots of object stores and weekly full snapshots of metadata; snapshots are tagged with region and tenant id.
- Snapshot storage: retained in the same cloud region by default (us-west-2 for Lucent).
- Snapshot purge flow: deletion request triggers a two-step workflow: 
  1) control-plane tombstone + enqueue purge job;
  2) worker processes remove objects and then mark snapshot metadata as deleted.
- RPO/RTO notes: RPO for hosted accounts is typically 24 hours; RTO targets vary by incident SLA.

Proof artifacts we can provide on request:
- Export of deletion audit (log lines) showing purge job timestamps.
- Snapshot manifest evidencing snapshot IDs removed.
- Redacted example of purge job runbook.

Edge cases to call out:
- If customer uses third-party connectors (e.g., S3 forwarders), object custody may involve third-party retention rules — we recommend including connector configs in the scope of erasure.
- Cached model KV entries: small prefix caches may persist briefly after deletion until cache eviction runs; cache invalidation is part of the purge job.

Estimated timelines (conservative):
- Primary store purge: 1-7 business days.
- Snapshot purge (automatic schedule): up to 30 days; expedited on contract -> 5-7 business days.

I'll attach a short playbook doc (redwood-ttl-playbook.docx) as a reference.

-Kim
